transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 21.91)"><g class="ltx_tikzmatrix_row" transform="matrix(1 0 0 1 0 9.61)"><g class="ltx_tikzmatrix_col ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:4.61em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="9.61" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)" width="63.77"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S2.F2.pic1.19" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">to Decoder</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g><g class="ltx_tikzmatrix_row" transform="matrix(1 0 0 1 0 19.22)"><g class="ltx_tikzmatrix_col ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:2.6em;--ltx-fo-height:0.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.3" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.61)" width="36.02"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S2.F2.pic1.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">Layer </span><math id="S2.F2.pic1.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></g></g></g></g></svg></span>
</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>Overview of ECHO. The backbone’s final decoder layer <math id="S2.F2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> and output head are reused to predict every future horizon. Dynamic Depth Sampling (DDS) draws one prediction depth <math id="S2.F2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\sim\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\sim\pi</annotation></semantics></math> per optimizer step, with probabilities that decay along depth. Green blocks denote layers shared with the backbone.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first show that final-layer sharing benefits the backbone through direct multi-horizon supervision, and then dynamic depth sampling makes it affordable at greater depth.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We show that reusing the backbone’s final layer turns multi-horizon supervision into a direct training signal: downstream performance improves over auxiliary MTP, and shows further gains at greater depth.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Causal Self-Recursion:</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">we follow the autoregressive design of DeepSeek-V3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> to preserve causal dependency, where each additional horizon is predicted from the previous final-layer hidden state <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{L}_{t-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{L}_{t-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and the embedding <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e(y_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e(y_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> of the previously predicted token. As shown in <a href="#S2.F2" title="In 2.3 Looped Transformers ‣ 2 Related Work ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>,
rather than attaching a dedicated module for each depth, we recursively apply the backbone’s final decoder layer <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{L}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>L</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{L}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> and output head at every horizon, connected to the previous step by a lightweight fusion layer <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{L}_{t}=\begin{cases}h^{L}_{1},&amp;t=1,\\
T^{L}\big(F\left(h^{L}_{t-1},e(x_{t})\right)\big),&amp;t&gt;1,\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>L</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>L</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mi>L</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{L}_{t}=\begin{cases}h^{L}_{1},&amp;t=1,\\
T^{L}\big(F\left(h^{L}_{t-1},e(x_{t})\right)\big),&amp;t&gt;1,\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">apart from the lightweight fusion layer, every parameter used for future prediction is also used for next-token generation. Supervision from every horizon shapes the backbone directly, and the same layer can be applied repeatedly to draft beyond the trained depth.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We show two benefits of the resulting direct multi-horizon supervision:</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sharing improves downstream performance, especially in reasoning capability.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To isolate the effect of sharing, we compare ECHO with DeepSeek’s MTP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> at matched prediction depth (<a href="#S3.F3.sf1" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(a)</span></a>).
Under this comparison, sharing the final layer gives ECHO the lead at depth 1, most clearly on math, reasoning and code (<math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.79" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.79</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.79</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.57</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.57</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.35</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.35</annotation></semantics></math>), and it reaches <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+2.63" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2.63</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+2.63</annotation></semantics></math> on reasoning and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+2.23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2.23</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+2.23</annotation></semantics></math> on code at depth 3.
The difference lies in where multi-horizon supervision mainly lands.
With auxiliary modules, the signal is largely absorbed by the modules dedicated to individual horizons, leaving the backbone’s hidden layers specialized for the next token <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mehra et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Sharing removes this bottleneck by construction: since the final layer predicts every horizon, supervision from all horizons is concentrated on the parameters that generate the next token.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To examine how each design uses added depth, we compare each family with itself from depth 1 to depth 3.
Averaged over all fourteen benchmarks, deeper supervision improves ECHO by <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.63" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.63</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.63</annotation></semantics></math> points, whereas DeepSeek’s MTP gains only <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.16</annotation></semantics></math>, and ECHO’s advantage on reasoning and code persists as depth increases (<a href="#S3.F3.sf1" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(a)</span></a>).
This divergence follows from where each new horizon’s loss goes: in ECHO it reaches the backbone directly, whereas in DeepSeek’s MTP it mostly trains the newly added module, as discussed above.
This explains why auxiliary MTP rarely goes deeper in practice: DeepSeek-V3 trains with a single MTP module <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, and MiMo finds that adding MTP layers brings no further improvement <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">LLM-Core Xiaomi, 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="S3.F3.2" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><span id="S3.F3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_align_stretched ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;"></span></p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="S3.F3.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.24766v1/figure3a.svg" id="S3.F3.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/449;" width="476" height="449"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(a) </span>In pretraining, the gain concentrates on reasoning and code, and grows with depth.</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="S3.F3.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.24766v1/figure3b.svg" id="S3.F3.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/449;" width="476" height="449"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(b) </span>At inference, it keeps the longest accepted length, widening with entropy.</figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span><span id="S3.F3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">What final-layer sharing buys, in pretraining and at inference.</span>
(a) Mean per-task score difference from MTP-1 within each task category, over the
fourteen benchmarks of <a href="#A3.T1" title="In Appendix C Full Benchmark Results ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, with the category size below
each label and the fourteen-task averages in the legend.
(b) Accepted length at <math id="S3.F3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> with rejection sampling, against the target’s
predictive entropy; the warm-start EAGLE-3 drafter is trained from DeepSeek’s MTP
baseline, following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kimi Team (2026)</a></cite>.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Affordable Long-Horizon Supervision via Dynamic Depth Sampling (DDS)</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We show that dynamically sampling the training depth lowers the cost of long-horizon supervision without sacrificing its gains in downstream performance and drafting quality.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dynamic Depth Sampling.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At each optimizer step, DDS draws a prediction depth <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\sim\pi(k)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\sim\pi(k)</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\dots,K\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\dots,K\}</annotation></semantics></math> and unrolls the recursion of equation <a href="#S3.E1" title="Equation 1 ‣ Causal Self-Recursion: ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> for depths <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> through <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S2.F2" title="In 2.3 Looped Transformers ‣ 2 Related Work ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), so the MTP training overhead scales with the expected depth</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[D]=\sum_{k=1}^{K}k\,\pi(k)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[D]=\sum_{k=1}^{K}k\,\pi(k).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">In practice, we use <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi=(0.6,0.3,0.1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi=(0.6,0.3,0.1)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}3</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[D]=1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[D]=1.5</annotation></semantics></math>, half the overhead of training all three depths.
Throughout, this <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">MTP training overhead</em> is reported in units of the depth-1 module, that is, unrolls of the shared layer per optimizer step; it is the increment on top of the backbone, not the end-to-end cost of a training step.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">DDS lowers the MTP training overhead while preserving downstream benefit.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">ECHO-1.5<sup id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> matches ECHO-3 on the benchmark average (<math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="36.34" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>36.34</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36.34</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="36.36" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>36.36</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36.36</annotation></semantics></math>, <a href="#S3.F3.sf1" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(a)</span></a>) at half the MTP training overhead.
This holds because DDS changes how often each depth is trained, not which depths are trained.
Since depths are sampled from <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,2,3\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,2,3\}</annotation></semantics></math>, ECHO-1.5<sup id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> still receives depth-3 supervision, only not at every step, so it keeps the benefit of long-horizon supervision without unrolling every depth in every batch.
Because deeper horizons condition on longer chains of recursive hidden states, their supervision grows noisier with depth, so DDS concentrates training on reliable shallow positions and protects the shared backbone from deep-horizon noise, much as stochastic depth trains deeper layers less often <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2016</a>)</cite>.
At this cost, ECHO-1.5<sup id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> also outperforms MTP-1 on math, reasoning and code (<math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.00" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.00</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.00</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.31" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.31</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.31</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+2.37" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2.37</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+2.37</annotation></semantics></math>) and still leads MTP-3 at twice its budget (<math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.55" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.55</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.55</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+2.31" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2.31</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+2.31</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.67" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.67</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.67</annotation></semantics></math>; <a href="#S3.F3.sf1" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figures</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(a)</span></a> and <a href="#A3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Appendix C Full Benchmark Results ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We analyze how ECHO’s end-to-end paradigm intrinsically aligns the drafter with the target, entirely eliminating the need for post-hoc drafter finetuning.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Training Shallow, Drafting Deep</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first show how DDS aligns training with the acceptance dynamics of speculative decoding, then demonstrate how last-layer sharing enables depth extrapolation beyond the trained depth.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">DDS aligns training with speculative decoding.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At inference, the drafter proposes <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> tokens and the target verifies them in parallel, but draft tokens are committed only up to the first rejection <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leviathan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
With acceptance rate <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}\in(0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}\in(0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> at position <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, position <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is reached with probability <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}a_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}a_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, so the expected accepted length is</p>
<table id="S4.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\tau]=1+\sum_{d=1}^{K}\prod_{i=1}^{d}a_{i}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>d</mi></munderover><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\tau]=1+\sum_{d=1}^{K}\prod_{i=1}^{d}a_{i},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is the accepted length, the bonus token plus the accepted drafts.
A rejection at depth <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> thus truncates the <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{k}=K-k+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{k}=K-k+1</annotation></semantics></math> drafts at and after it, so shallow depths dominate accepted length.
DDS effectively trains depth <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> with a frequency that decays along depth,</p>
<table id="S4.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{k}=\mathbb{P}(D\geq k)=\sum_{j=k}^{K}\pi(j)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{k}=\mathbb{P}(D\geq k)=\sum_{j=k}^{K}\pi(j),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">so <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi=(0.6,0.3,0.1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi=(0.6,0.3,0.1)</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=(1,0.4,0.1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f=(1,0.4,0.1)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Under lossless verification, the rejection rate is <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-a_{k}=\mathrm{TV}(p_{k},q_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-a_{k}=\mathrm{TV}(p_{k},q_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leviathan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
LK losses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">Samarin et al., 2026</a>)</cite> exploit this identity to optimize acceptance directly, but treat each position equally.
Instead, relating the rejection rate to the data distribution <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and accounting for truncation across depths gives (<a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>)</p>
<table id="S4.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\tau]\ \geq\ 1+K-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f)\ \geq\ 1+K-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\mathbf{1})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo rspace="0.500em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo rspace="0.500em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\tau]\ \geq\ 1+K-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f)\ \geq\ 1+K-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\mathbf{1}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f)=\sqrt{\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2}/f_{k}}\,\sqrt{\sum_{k}f_{k}\mathrm{KL}(d_{k}\,\|\,q_{k})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>f</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>KL</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><mi>q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f)=\sqrt{\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2}/f_{k}}\,\sqrt{\sum_{k}f_{k}\mathrm{KL}(d_{k}\,\|\,q_{k})}</annotation></semantics></math> bounds the MTP loss.
The last inequality compares DDS with the uniform depth supervision (<math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=\mathbf{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f=\mathbf{1}</annotation></semantics></math>) and holds for schedules that decay toward the optimum (<a href="#A2.Thmtheorem1" title="Proposition B.1. ‣ Derivation of . ‣ Appendix B Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>).
The uniform depth supervision weights every depth’s error equally, whereas decaying <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> tightens the bound, so reducing the training loss translates more directly into accepted length.
DDS thus concentrates target-draft alignment on the shallow depths that determine acceptance, preserving accepted length despite reduced supervision at greater depths.
Existing drafters encode this decay by reweighting the loss while still training every depth at every step <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>)</cite>;
DDS instead encodes it in how often each depth is trained, so the training compute follows the decay.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Extrapolating Beyond the Training Horizon.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We refer to drafting beyond the maximum depth seen during training as <em id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">depth extrapolation</em>. As shown in <a href="#S1.F1.sf2" title="In Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1(b)</span></a>, beyond the trained depth (<math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math>), ECHO keeps gaining at a nearly constant rate, and ECHO-1.5<sup id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> retains this gain at half the MTP training overhead of ECHO-3, whereas the gains of MTP-3 shrink with each step and saturate. Sharing also makes extrapolation the natural complement to DDS: training concentrates supervision on shallow depths, and recursion carries it to deeper ones at inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Staying Aligned under realistic setting</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We then show that ECHO outperforms existing post-hoc drafters, with larger gains on high-entropy, realistic, and open-ended tasks, thanks to two complementary factors: causal drafting ensures consistency among draft tokens, while joint pretraining aligns the draft distribution with the target.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="S4.F4.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.24766v1/figure4a.svg" id="S4.F4.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/472;" width="476" height="472"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(a) </span>Deeper sampling trails ECHO-1.5<sup id="S4.F4.sf1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S4.F4.sf1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> before finetuning.</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="S4.F4.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.24766v1/figure4b.svg" id="S4.F4.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/472;" width="476" height="472"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(b) </span>Finetuning widens the lead on both classes.</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="S4.F4.sf3" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.24766v1/figure4c.svg" id="S4.F4.sf3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/472;" width="476" height="472"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(c) </span>The lead against the spread two matched runs measure.</figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span><span id="S4.F4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The advantage persists under deeper sampling, supervised finetuning
and a doubled token budget.</span> Mean
per-task gain over the matched DeepSeek baseline, by task class: MTP-1 before
finetuning, MTP-1-Instruct after it. (<a href="#S4.F4.sf3" title="Figure 4(c) ‣ Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Staying Aligned under realistic setting ‣ 4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4(c)</span></a>) shows the gap at
step 78k and at step 156k, and the error bars are the run-to-run standard deviation
from an independent repeat of the 78k recipe, <math id="S4.F4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.08" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.08</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.08</annotation></semantics></math> on reasoning &amp; code and
<math id="S4.F4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.38</annotation></semantics></math> on QA &amp; multiple choice. Doubling the budget moves
the reasoning &amp; code gap by <math id="S4.F4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01</annotation></semantics></math>, a sixth of that spread, whereas the repeat
moves the QA &amp; multiple choice gap by <math id="S4.F4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.54" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.54</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.54</annotation></semantics></math>, more than its own. The reasoning &amp; code
advantage therefore survives both conditions and the run-to-run spread, while the
QA &amp; multiple choice difference stays inside it.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Causal Drafting Matters in Open-Ended Generation.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#S3.F3.sf2" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(b)</span></a>, ECHO and other causal drafters outperform parallel drafters on high-entropy tasks, consistent with <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2026)</a></cite>; <a href="#A9.F8" title="In Appendix I Artifact Licensing ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> shows the same ordering in decode speedup.
When the next tokens are uncertain, the target’s choice is hard to anticipate, so the probability of acceptance falls off steeply with depth and most of a long draft is discarded.
A causal drafter adapts to this by extending its draft step by step, while a parallel drafter emits a fixed-length block whose deeper tokens are mostly rejected at verification.
The balance shifts on simple code and mathematics benchmarks such as HumanEval, MBPP, and GSM8K, where long stretches of output are determined by syntax or derivation, and block-parallel drafting becomes worthwhile <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, whereas realistic software engineering tasks such as SWE-bench remain high-entropy and still favor causal drafting (<a href="#S3.F3.sf2" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(b)</span></a>).
Such simple tasks, however, are a small fraction of real-world usage, account for under 8% of consumer ChatGPT messages, while open-ended practical guidance, information seeking, and writing account for nearly 80% <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chatterji et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Joint Pretraining Closes the Alignment Gap.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Acceptance depends on how closely the draft distribution matches the target’s <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leviathan et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and a drafter can better match the target where it has seen the target’s data. ECHO is trained with the target end-to-end and sees its full pretraining corpus. In contrast, auxiliary drafters are fit to a frozen target on a small finetuning set, so their acceptance drops under distribution shift <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hong et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
The EAGLE-3 pair in <a href="#S3.F3.sf2" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(b)</span></a> isolates this effect: with architecture and finetuning data held fixed, warm-started EAGLE-3 achieves a longer accepted length than its cold-start counterpart, consistent with recent findings that pretrained initialization strengthens drafters, most on out-of-domain inputs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bie et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
Yet on open-ended tasks, warm-starting still falls short of ECHO, with the largest gap on SWE-bench.
ECHO is instead optimized jointly with the target on every pretraining update, so its alignment is maintained throughout training, in line with the high acceptance rates reported for MTP modules trained jointly during pretraining <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">LLM-Core Xiaomi, 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>The Advantage Holds across Data, Depth and Runs</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We finally examine whether ECHO’s advantage holds along three axes: more pretraining data, deeper sampling, and repeated runs.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Scaling with Data</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ECHO’s advantage persists with more pretraining data.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We extend pretraining of ECHO-1 and DeepSeek’s MTP-1 from step 78k to step 156k, doubling the token budget.
Both models improve, and ECHO-1 keeps its lead over DeepSeek’s MTP-1 measured at the same step: <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.52</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.52</annotation></semantics></math> at step 78k and <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.50</annotation></semantics></math> at step 156k, and on reasoning &amp; code it is <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.88" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.88</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.88</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.89" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.89</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.89</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S4.F4.sf3" title="In Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Staying Aligned under realistic setting ‣ 4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4(c)</span></a>, <a href="#A4.T2" title="In Twice the training budget. ‣ Appendix D Stability across Pretraining Runs ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).
This indicates that ECHO’s advantage is stable under data scaling rather than an early-training effect that more data would erase.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Scaling with Depth</h3>

<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ECHO’s advantage holds across sampling depths.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next train ECHO-2<sup id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(7)</span></sup>, which samples <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\dots,7\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\dots,7\}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[D]=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[D]=2</annotation></semantics></math>, at <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4/3</annotation></semantics></math> the MTP training overhead of ECHO-1.5<sup id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup>.
It trails ECHO-1.5<sup id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> in pretraining but overtakes it after SFT by 0.49, reaching the largest lead over DeepSeek’s MTP-Instruct of any configuration (<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+2.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+2.10</annotation></semantics></math>; <a href="#A6.T3" title="In Appendix F After Supervised Finetuning ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).
The gap in pretraining may be due to errors accumulating at deeper positions, which makes their supervision noisier and draws training away from the reliable shallow depths.
After SFT, however, the deeper supervision appears to pay off, possibly because finetuning makes better use of what the backbone learned.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Stability across Runs</h3>

<section id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ECHO’s lead is robust to training and evaluation noise.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A reported gap can come from noise rather than the method itself.
We eliminate evaluation noise by decoding greedily, so the remaining source is training.
To measure it, we pretrain ECHO-1 and DeepSeek’s MTP-1 a second time under the same recipe and compare the two runs at the same step.
Across the two runs, ECHO leads DeepSeek’s MTP-1 by <math id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.52</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.52</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.78" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.78</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.78</annotation></semantics></math>, and its lead on reasoning &amp; code shifts by only <math id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.11</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S4.F4.sf3" title="In Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Staying Aligned under realistic setting ‣ 4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4(c)</span></a>; <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Stability across Pretraining Runs ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>).
ECHO’s overall and reasoning &amp; code leads are therefore reproducible across runs.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Experiment Setup</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Full architecture, prompt, scoring and speculative decoding details are given in <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Experiment Setup ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Models and Baselines</span>: Every configuration shares a 10B-A1B Latent MoE backbone <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Blakeman et al., 2025</a>)</cite> with 24 layers, multi-head latent attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, and 256 routed experts with eight active per token <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, trained under the same recipe so that the comparison isolates the MTP design.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pretraining</span>: 600B tokens at sequence length 4,096 and batch size 1,920 in bfloat16 with Muon <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jordan et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, on 24 nodes of eight H800 GPUs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Depth Sampling</span>: ECHO-1.5<sup id="S6.p4.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S6.p4.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> samples <math id="S6.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="S6.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,2,3\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,2,3\}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S6.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi=(0.6,0.3,0.1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi=(0.6,0.3,0.1)</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math id="S6.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[D]=1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[D]=1.5</annotation></semantics></math> and ECHO-2<sup id="S6.p4.1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S6.p4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(7)</span></sup> samples over <math id="S6.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,\dots,7\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,\dots,7\}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S6.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi=(0.520,0.220,0.121,0.068,0.036,0.019,0.016)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.520</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.220</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.121</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.068</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.036</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.019</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.016</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi=(0.520,0.220,0.121,0.068,0.036,0.019,0.016)</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math id="S6.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[D]=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[D]=2</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Supervised Finetuning</span>: Every configuration is finetuned with the same recipe, 5,000 steps over one pass of an in-house chat corpus at context length 32,768, keeping its pretrained MTP depths.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Computational Cost</span>:
Each pretraining run takes approximately 3 days on 192 NVIDIA H800 GPUs with a global batch size of 1,920, followed by 5 hours of SFT on the same hardware. Post-hoc drafter training uses 24 H800 GPUs with a global batch size of 48, requiring about 22 hours for EAGLE-3, 19 hours for DFlash, and 55 hours for DSpark.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Benchmark Evaluation</span>: Fourteen few-shot <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brown et al., 2020</a>)</cite> benchmarks decoded greedily, grouped by task form into mathematics, reasoning, multi-subject multiple choice, code and closed-book question answering, with CoT prompting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2022</a>)</cite> on MATH, GSM8K and BBH.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Speculative decoding:</span> We adopt the same temperature setting (<math id="S6.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=1</annotation></semantics></math>) for both the target and draft models, following Bebop <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026b</a>)</cite> and GLM-5.2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">GLM Team, 2026</a>)</cite>. This matters for RL training: rejection sampling with draft temperature<math id="S6.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> keeps acceptance stable as target entropy rises, whereas greedy drafting degrades sharply at higher temperatures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026b</a>)</cite>. All drafters are served with SGLang on a single node of eight H800 GPUs and budget-matched at seven proposed positions plus one bonus token per verification step. We report decode-only throughput and mean accepted length on ten tasks, split by the target model’s predictive entropy into predictable and open-ended groups.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented ECHO, which turns multi-token prediction from an auxiliary task into part of the autoregressive objective.
By reusing the backbone’s own final layer at every horizon, ECHO lets multi-horizon supervision shape the parameters that generate the next token, and Dynamic Depth Sampling makes deeper horizons affordable by training them less often.
Unlike auxiliary MTP such as DeepSeek, ECHO improves with added depth, and ECHO-1.5<sup id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="S7.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> matches the downstream gain of ECHO-3 at half the MTP overhead.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At inference, the same shared layer makes the pretrained model its own drafter with close draft-target alignment: it drafts beyond its trained depth where auxiliary modules saturate, and it outperforms post-hoc drafters on open-ended, high-entropy generation.
This advantage holds under a doubled token budget, a repeated pretraining run, and supervised finetuning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Limitations</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Due to compute constraints, pretraining was repeated once and finetuning was run with a single seed.
How far the gains from added depth and from depth extrapolation extend, how DDS behaves at greater depths, and why deeper sampling pays off only after finetuning are left to future work.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
