<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Experiment Setup</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Pretraining</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Model Architecture</span>: The backbone is a 10B-A1B Latent Mixture-of-Experts transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Blakeman et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, that is 10B parameters in total with 1B activated per token, stacked as 24 layers of hidden size 1,024 with 16 attention heads. Attention is multi-head latent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, with 512-dimensional query and key–value latents, and we add gated attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qiu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, per-head query–key normalization and rotary positional embeddings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Su et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Every layer is a mixture of experts in a latent space: the expert block projects the hidden state down to 512 dimensions, runs 256 fine-grained routed experts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2024</a>)</cite> of intermediate size 1,024 there, and projects back, with the router reading the hidden state rather than the latent. A sigmoid gate sends each token to eight routed experts, balanced by a sequence-level auxiliary loss, plus one shared expert. The SwiGLU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shazeer, 2020</a>)</cite> feed-forward width is 5,120 and the vocabulary holds 201,216 tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Training Settings</span>: We train the model on 600B tokens with a context sequence length of 4,096 and a global batch size of 1,920. Training uses bfloat16 precision and the Muon optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jordan et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, with AdamW retained for the embeddings, the biases, the output head and the expert router, a learning rate of <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, a warmup of 1,000 steps, weight decay of <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, and gradient clipping at <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>. Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2024a)</a></cite>, we set the MTP loss scaling factor to <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math>. Pretraining runs on 24 nodes of eight H800 GPUs each, with eight-way expert parallelism, stage-one optimizer sharding, no tensor or pipeline parallelism, and full activation recomputation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Computational Cost</span>:
Each pretraining run is conducted on 24 nodes with eight NVIDIA H800 80GB GPUs per node (192 GPUs in total), taking approximately three days to complete. Supervised finetuning uses the same hardware configuration and takes approximately five hours per run.
For the post-hoc speculative decoding baselines, we train the draft models on three nodes (24 H800 80GB GPUs), using a global batch size of 48. EAGLE-3 (cold-start and warm-start) and DFlash use a per-GPU batch size of 2 without gradient accumulation, whereas DSpark uses a per-GPU batch size of 1 with two gradient accumulation steps due to GPU memory constraints. EAGLE-3 requires approximately 22 hours per run in measured wall-clock time. Based on the recorded compute time and an estimated 1.27<math id="A1.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> overhead for startup, checkpointing, and cluster variability, DSpark requires approximately 55 hours, while DFlash requires approximately 19 hours.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Methods Compared</span>: All six configurations are trained under the recipe above, so the comparison isolates the MTP design. ECHO reuses the backbone’s last layer as the body of every MTP depth; DeepSeek’s MTP baselines follow <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2024a)</a></cite> and keep an independent module per depth, sharing only the embedding and the output head. ECHO-1 and MTP-1 train one depth, ECHO-3 and MTP-3 train three at every step, ECHO-1.5<sup id="A1.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> samples depths one to three with <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[D]=1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[D]=1.5</annotation></semantics></math>, and ECHO-2<sup id="A1.SS1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(7)</span></sup> extends dynamic depth sampling to depths one through seven with <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[D]=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[D]=2</annotation></semantics></math>. The two cost-matched comparisons are ECHO-1 against MTP-1 at equal depth-one cost, and ECHO-1.5<sup id="A1.SS1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A1.SS1.p4.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> against MTP-3 at half the MTP cost.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic Depth Sampling</span>: The sampled depth is <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\sim\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\sim\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> places probabilities 0.6, 0.3 and 0.1 on depths 1, 2 and 3, so <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[D]=1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[D]=1.5</annotation></semantics></math>. Each optimizer step draws one <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> and trains depths 1 through <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>, and every micro-batch in the step shares the same <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>, which keeps per-step compute constant. Averaging the loss over the <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> trained depths gives depth <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> the weight <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}\{D\geq d\}/D]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}\{D\geq d\}/D]</annotation></semantics></math>, and these weights sum to one: ECHO reweights depths by how often it samples them, not by attaching a per-depth loss coefficient. <math id="A1.SS1.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> is a deterministic function of the seed and the step index, so every rank derives it without communication and a resumed run continues the same sequence.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Supervised Finetuning</span>: All configurations adopt an identical recipe: 5,000 steps over one pass of an in-house chat SFT corpus at a context length of 32,768, with eight-way context parallelism. Each keeps the MTP depths it was pretrained with, so the finetuned comparison isolates the same design difference as the pretrained one.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Benchmark Evaluation</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Evaluation Setup</span>: We evaluate the pretrained checkpoints on fourteen few-shot benchmarks, grouped by the form of the task following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2024a)</a></cite>: mathematics with MATH <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., 2021b</a>)</cite> and GSM8K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cobbe et al., 2021</a>)</cite>; reasoning with BBH <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Suzgun et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, BBEH <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kazemi et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, WinoGrande <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sakaguchi et al., 2021</a>)</cite> and PIQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bisk et al., 2020</a>)</cite>; multi-subject multiple choice with MMLU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hendrycks et al., 2021a</a>)</cite> and MMLU-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>; code with HumanEval+ and MBPP+ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and LiveCodeBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jain et al., 2025</a>)</cite>; closed-book question answering with PopQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mallen et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, PreciseWikiQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and HotpotQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2018</a>)</cite>. We report unweighted averages within each group and across all fourteen benchmarks. Benchmarks such as GPQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rein et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, SimpleQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and HMMT are left out for lack of resolution rather than for any defect in their scoring: every configuration scores near their floor, so the row moves more than it resolves.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Prompts and Decoding</span>: All benchmarks are evaluated in the few-shot in-context format <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brown et al., 2020</a>)</cite>. Chain-of-thought prompting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2022</a>)</cite> is used on MATH, GSM8K and BBH, with eight, eight and four demonstrations respectively. The remaining benchmarks are prompted to answer directly, with five demonstrations for the multiple-choice benchmarks, ten for closed-book question answering and two for BBEH. BBH is released under both a chain-of-thought and an answer-directly prompt over the same items for examining the chain-of-thought effect <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Suzgun et al., 2023</a>)</cite>; we report its chain-of-thought form in the main results. Decoding is greedy throughout. Generation is capped per benchmark: two tokens for MMLU and eleven for MMLU-Pro, which are answered with a single option label; <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>65</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65</annotation></semantics></math> for the closed-book sets and <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="101" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>101</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">101</annotation></semantics></math> for PopQA; <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="401" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>401</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">401</annotation></semantics></math> for MATH, <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math> for GSM8K, BBEH and HumanEval+, <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="601" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>601</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">601</annotation></semantics></math> for BBH, <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>768</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">768</annotation></semantics></math> for LiveCodeBench and <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8192</annotation></semantics></math> for MBPP+. WinoGrande and PIQA involve no generation. Stop sequences are applied when the answer is extracted rather than during decoding, so the cap is what bounds each output.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Scoring and Averaging</span>: Each benchmark’s score is an unweighted macro-average over its sub-tasks rather than a per-item micro-average. Four scoring rules are used, one per group of benchmarks. GSM8K, MATH, BBH, MMLU and MMLU-Pro are scored by rule from the extracted answer. HumanEval+, MBPP+ and LiveCodeBench are scored as pass@1 by execution <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. WinoGrande and PIQA are scored by length-normalized log-likelihood over the candidate continuations rather than by generation, as in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2024a)</a></cite>, with the normalization of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al. (2024)</a></cite>. PreciseWikiQA, HotpotQA, PopQA and BBEH are graded against the reference answer by an LLM judge. In <a href="#A3.T1" title="In Appendix C Full Benchmark Results ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> the three factual-knowledge sets are graded by gpt-oss-120b and BBEH by Claude Opus 4.8; in <a href="#A6.T3" title="In Appendix F After Supervised Finetuning ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> all four are graded by Claude Opus 4.8. Of these, the three factual-knowledge sets report the F1 of overall accuracy and accuracy among attempted items, with abstentions in the denominator of the former only. Category averages and the overall figure are unweighted means over benchmarks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Speculative Decoding under Serving</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Serving Stack</span>: All serving measurements use SGLang on one node of eight H800 GPUs, with tensor parallelism 8 and FlashAttention-3.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Drafters</span>: All drafters are budget-matched at seven proposed positions plus one target bonus token, i.e. eight verification slots per request per step. ECHO reuses the target’s final layer and full output head. EAGLE-3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>)</cite> uses one draft layer with a reduced 32,000-entry head scattered back to target width, in a cold-start and a warm-start variant; following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kimi Team (2026)</a></cite>, the warm start initializes the draft from DeepSeek’s pretrained MTP weights, and is always normalized by the baseline of its own run. DSpark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>)</cite> and DFlash <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2026</a>)</cite> are block-parallel with five draft layers, the former adding a low-rank Markov transition bias.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Serving Metric</span>: We report decode-only throughput, decoded tokens over summed per-request decode latency, which excludes prefill; metrics that include prefill confound the comparison across tasks with differing prompt lengths. Speedup is recomputed against the baseline of the same run, and accepted length is decoded tokens per verification step.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Tasks</span>: Serving results use ten tasks in two groups, split by predictive entropy as in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2026)</a></cite>. Predictable, following the commonly adopted SpecForge benchmarks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>: HumanEval, MBPP, MATH-500, GSM8K, LiveCodeBench. Open-ended: SWE-bench, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench, summarization, Alpaca. Question answering, retrieval-augmented generation, translation and AIME-25 are excluded, all having median outputs of twenty to thirty tokens, too few verification steps for a stable decode-only ratio. The entropy axis is the target’s own predictive entropy, measured separately.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Verification Budget</span>: DSpark is evaluated with its confidence scheduler disabled, verifying the full draft block at every step, as in the diagnostic baseline of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al. (2026)</a></cite>. The scheduler is a calibrated cost model rather than a threshold: it needs a latency curve re-profiled for each GPU and backend <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, and a confidence head calibrated on the serving distribution, since the survival probabilities it multiplies must be absolute rather than merely well-ranked. That calibration does not transfer, because the mechanism assumes acceptance varies sharply across domains in the first place. With the head enabled but neither artifact available, per-step cost rose 5–14% and nothing was pruned.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Depth Extrapolation</span>: The depth sweep of <a href="#S1.F1.sf2" title="In Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1(b)</span></a> uses a separate harness. We report the accepted length obtained at serving depth <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{K}=1+\sum_{j\leq K}\prod_{i\leq j}p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{K}=1+\sum_{j\leq K}\prod_{i\leq j}p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, for conditional acceptance rate <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> at depth <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. The expression is exact rather than a fit: the draft loop reaches depth <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i+1</annotation></semantics></math> only after depth <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> is accepted, so <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\prod_{i\leq j}p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\prod_{i\leq j}p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the probability that the first <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> drafted tokens are all accepted, and summing those probabilities gives their expected number. Runs use draft depth <math id="A1.SS3.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}7</annotation></semantics></math>, greedy on both sides, 256 new tokens, and pool GSM8K, HumanEval and MATH-500 weighted by rounds.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> be the target, draft, and data next-token distributions at depth <math id="A2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, each conditioned on the current prefix.
Let <math id="A2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=1-a_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=1-a_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{k}=K-k+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{k}=K-k+1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="A_{k}=\mathrm{KL}(d_{k}\,\|\,q_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{k}=\mathrm{KL}(d_{k}\,\|\,q_{k})</annotation></semantics></math>, the drafter distributional loss at depth <math id="A2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>.
We assume the drafter is trained on target-generated data, so <math id="A2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}=p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}=p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.p1.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="A_{k}=\mathrm{KL}(p_{k}\,\|\,q_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{k}=\mathrm{KL}(p_{k}\,\|\,q_{k})</annotation></semantics></math>.
All quantities are averaged over prefixes, which we assume follow the training data distribution at inference; each inequality below holds pointwise for every prefix and therefore after averaging, with Jensen’s inequality moving the average inside square roots where needed.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Derivation of <a href="#S4.E5" title="In DDS aligns training with speculative decoding. ‣ 4.1 Training Shallow, Drafting Deep ‣ 4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The full chain is</p>

<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=\sum_{k}c_{k}\sqrt{A_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=\sum_{k}c_{k}\sqrt{A_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(i) Union bound.</em>
By <a href="#S4.E3" title="In DDS aligns training with speculative decoding. ‣ 4.1 Training Shallow, Drafting Deep ‣ 4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1+K-\mathbb{E}[\tau]=\sum_{d=1}^{K}\bigl(1-\prod_{i\leq d}(1-\delta_{i})\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1+K-\mathbb{E}[\tau]=\sum_{d=1}^{K}\bigl(1-\prod_{i\leq d}(1-\delta_{i})\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math>, where each term is the probability that draft <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is not accepted.
The probability of at least one rejection among depths <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1,\dots,d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,\dots,d</annotation></semantics></math> is at most <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i\leq d}\delta_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i\leq d}\delta_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, a bound tight up to second-order terms in <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.
Summing over <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, each <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is counted once for each of the <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> values <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\geq k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\geq k</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{k}=\mathrm{TV}(p_{k},q_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{k}=\mathrm{TV}(p_{k},q_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> under lossless verification <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leviathan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(ii) Pinsker’s inequality.</em>
Since <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}=p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}=p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, Pinsker’s inequality gives <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{TV}(p_{k},q_{k})=\mathrm{TV}(d_{k},q_{k})\leq\sqrt{A_{k}/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{TV}(p_{k},q_{k})=\mathrm{TV}(d_{k},q_{k})\leq\sqrt{A_{k}/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(iii) Cauchy–Schwarz.</em>
Writing <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{k}\sqrt{A_{k}}=(c_{k}/\sqrt{f_{k}})\cdot\sqrt{f_{k}A_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{k}\sqrt{A_{k}}=(c_{k}/\sqrt{f_{k}})\cdot\sqrt{f_{k}A_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A2.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q\ \leq\ \mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f)=\sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{c_{k}^{2}}{f_{k}}}\ \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^{K}f_{k}A_{k}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0.778em" rspace="0.778em">≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mfrac><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q\ \leq\ \mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f)=\sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{c_{k}^{2}}{f_{k}}}\ \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^{K}f_{k}A_{k}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">with equality if and only if <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{k}\propto c_{k}/\sqrt{A_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∝</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{k}\propto c_{k}/\sqrt{A_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Since <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\lambda f)=\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\lambda f)=\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f)</annotation></semantics></math> for any <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, schedules with different compute budgets can be compared directly.
For MTP-<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\mathbf{1})=\sqrt{\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2}}\,\sqrt{\sum_{k}A_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\mathbf{1})=\sqrt{\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2}}\,\sqrt{\sum_{k}A_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2}=K(K+1)(2K+1)/6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2}=K(K+1)(2K+1)/6</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(iv) Decayed schedules.</em>
This is <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem1" title="Proposition B.1. ‣ Derivation of . ‣ Appendix B Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>(c).</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition B.1</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Suppose <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;A_{1}\leq\dots\leq A_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;A_{1}\leq\dots\leq A_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{\star}_{k}\propto c_{k}/\sqrt{A_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>∝</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{\star}_{k}\propto c_{k}/\sqrt{A_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then
(a) <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly decreasing in <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>;
(b) <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\mathbf{1})&gt;Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\mathbf{1})&gt;Q</annotation></semantics></math>;
(c) for <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{(t)}_{k}=(f^{\star}_{k})^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{(t)}_{k}=(f^{\star}_{k})^{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f^{(t)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f^{(t)})</annotation></semantics></math> is nonincreasing in <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, from <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\mathbf{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">MTP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(\mathbf{1})</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">(a) <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly decreasing and <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\sqrt{A_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\sqrt{A_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math> is nonincreasing, both positive.
(b) By (a), <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>𝟏</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is not proportional to <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>, so equality in <a href="#A2.E7" title="In Derivation of . ‣ Appendix B Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> fails.
(c) With <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{k}=\log f^{\star}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{k}=\log f^{\star}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, the function <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="F(t)=2\log\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f^{(t)})=\log\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2}e^{-tu_{k}}+\log\sum_{k}A_{k}e^{tu_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>log</mi><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MTP</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>log</mi><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>log</mi><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(t)=2\log\mathcal{L}_{\text{MTP}}(f^{(t)})=\log\sum_{k}c_{k}^{2}e^{-tu_{k}}+\log\sum_{k}A_{k}e^{tu_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a sum of log-sum-exps of affine functions, hence convex, and is minimized at <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1</annotation></semantics></math> by the equality condition of <a href="#A2.E7" title="In Derivation of . ‣ Appendix B Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>; a convex function is nonincreasing to the left of its minimizer.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The assumption <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{1}\leq\dots\leq A_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{1}\leq\dots\leq A_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> reflects that acceptance decays with depth.
<a href="#A2.Thmtheorem1" title="Proposition B.1. ‣ Derivation of . ‣ Appendix B Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a> concerns how tightly the training loss bounds lost length; that DDS attains comparable <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\tau]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\tau]</annotation></semantics></math> at lower cost is verified empirically.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Data not generated by the target.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}\neq p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}\neq p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, step (ii) uses the triangle inequality <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{TV}(p_{k},q_{k})\leq\mathrm{TV}(d_{k},q_{k})+\mathrm{TV}(d_{k},p_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{TV}(p_{k},q_{k})\leq\mathrm{TV}(d_{k},q_{k})+\mathrm{TV}(d_{k},p_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> and Pinsker on both terms, which adds <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{k}c_{k}\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}(d_{k}\,\|\,p_{k})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{k}c_{k}\sqrt{\mathrm{KL}(d_{k}\,\|\,p_{k})}</annotation></semantics></math> to every bound in <a href="#A2.E6" title="In Derivation of . ‣ Appendix B Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.
This term depends on neither the drafter nor the schedule, so steps (iii), (iv), and <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem1" title="Proposition B.1. ‣ Derivation of . ‣ Appendix B Decayed Depth Supervision and Accepted Length ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a> are unchanged.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Full Benchmark Results</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A3.T1" title="In Appendix C Full Benchmark Results ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> gives the per-benchmark scores behind the category gains of <a href="#S3.F3.sf1" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(a)</span></a>, for all six pretrained configurations over the fourteen benchmarks of the reported scope.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Provenance of the cells</span>: nine of the fourteen rows are scored by us under the protocol of <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Experiment Setup ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>. The other five are reported by an internal evaluation platform and are reproduced here as it returned them: PreciseWikiQA, HotpotQA and PopQA, graded by gpt-oss-120b over its full sets of <math id="A3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7{,}405" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7,405</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7{,}405</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14{,}256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14,256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14{,}256</annotation></semantics></math> items, together with MATH (<math id="A3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4{,}739" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4,739</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4{,}739</annotation></semantics></math> items, scored by rule) and MBPP+ (<math id="A3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="378" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>378</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">378</annotation></semantics></math> items, scored by execution). That platform’s answer-extraction and judging rules are not published with this paper, so these five rows cannot be reproduced exactly from outside it. Our own runs of them exist but measure a different quantity — a different few-shot prefix, an answer-extraction rule that does not match on MATH, a weaker test bar on MBPP+, and a <math id="A3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="600" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>600</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">600</annotation></semantics></math>-item sample under a different judge on the three closed-book sets — so they are not offered as a second reading.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Stability across Pretraining Runs</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Two of the configurations were pretrained a second time under the same recipe, and the comparison survives it. Over the fourteen benchmarks of the reported scope, ECHO MTP-1 leads DeepSeek’s MTP-1 by 0.52 points in the baseline run and by 0.78 in the repeat. Reasoning (<math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.57</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.57</annotation></semantics></math> then <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.33" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.33</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.33</annotation></semantics></math>) and code (<math id="A4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.35" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.35</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.35</annotation></semantics></math> then <math id="A4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.69" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.69</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.69</annotation></semantics></math>) both grow, multi-subject multiple choice turns in ECHO’s favor (<math id="A4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.52</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.52</annotation></semantics></math> then <math id="A4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.30</annotation></semantics></math>), closed-book QA stays within a fifth of a point of zero in both, and mathematics is the one category that moves the other way (<math id="A4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.79" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.79</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.79</annotation></semantics></math> then <math id="A4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.73</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.73</annotation></semantics></math>). Two evaluations of the same weights differ by 0.27 points per benchmark, which puts the noise at 0.13 on a fourteen-benchmark gap and 0.30 on a category gap. <a href="#A4.T2" title="In Twice the training budget. ‣ Appendix D Stability across Pretraining Runs ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> gives the three column groups, and <a href="#S4.F4.sf3" title="In Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Staying Aligned under realistic setting ‣ 4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4(c)</span></a> draws the two classes with the spread these two runs measure.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Twice the training budget.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The baseline run was then carried to step <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="156{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>156,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">156{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> on both sides, twice its token budget. Over the fourteen rows ECHO’s lead holds, <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.52</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.52</annotation></semantics></math> at step 78k against <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.50</annotation></semantics></math> at step 156k, a change of <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.02</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.02</annotation></semantics></math> against a spread of <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.14</annotation></semantics></math> across rows, with seven rows in its favor at each step, and every bucket is reproduced to within <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.2</annotation></semantics></math> points. Doubling the budget therefore leaves both the overall gap and the category ordering where they were. Repeating the run reproduces the overall gap to <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.26" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.26</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.26</annotation></semantics></math> points but not its split across categories, which moves by <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.8</annotation></semantics></math> points.</p>
</div>
