<td id="A4.T2.2.17.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb">15.48</td>
<td id="A4.T2.2.17.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb">16.20</td>
<td id="A4.T2.2.17.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb">16.38</td>
<td id="A4.T2.2.17.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb">16.97</td></tr>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>One recipe under two perturbations, both against the same baseline. <span id="A4.T2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Baseline</span>
is the run reported in <a href="#A3.T1" title="In Appendix C Full Benchmark Results ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. <span id="A4.T2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Repeat run</span> is an independent
pretraining run of the same recipe at the same step. <span id="A4.T2.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Twice the budget</span> is the
baseline run continued to step 156k.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Next-Token Loss Does Not Separate the Two Objectives</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A5.F5" title="In Appendix E Next-Token Loss Does Not Separate the Two Objectives ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> separates the objective into its two terms. On the backbone’s next-token
loss the two runs are indistinguishable: the gap averages <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.004" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.004</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.004</annotation></semantics></math> over the 78k steps and stays
between <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.004" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.004</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.004</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.005" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.005</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.005</annotation></semantics></math> in every 10k-step window, with ECHO-1 marginally above MTP-1
throughout. The MTP loss carries a larger gap in the same direction, <math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.011" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.011</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.011</annotation></semantics></math> at step 78k.
On the same token budget the two objectives therefore arrive at the same next-token likelihood,
and neither margin is one the method is meant to win.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.24766v1/echo_vs_mtp1_trainloss.svg" id="A5.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/181;" width="476" height="181"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>Training loss of ECHO-1 and MTP-1 over the first 78k steps of the baseline run,
separated into the backbone’s next-token loss (left) and the MTP loss (right).
The logged objective is the weighted sum
<math id="A5.F5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{backbone}}+0.3\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MTP}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>backbone</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>0.3</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>MTP</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{backbone}}+0.3\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MTP}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the left
panel is recovered by subtracting the weighted MTP loss from it. Each curve is an
exponential moving average over all <math id="A5.F5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> logged steps, with no subsampling; the
vertical range is clipped to what the curves occupy after step 12k, so the first few
thousand steps run above the frame.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This is the expected outcome rather than a negative result. ECHO’s multi-horizon objective adds no
capacity to the next-token head; it changes what the shared representation is required to support.
In predicting the next token the model is held responsible for several future positions at once,
which constrains the hidden state towards features that stay predictive beyond one step. The effect
of such a constraint is regularization, and regularization does not surface in the quantity it
constrains: next-token cross-entropy is the term both objectives already optimize, so matching it
is the premise of the comparison rather than its outcome. The two configurations separate
downstream instead, in the benchmark gaps of <a href="#A3.T1" title="In Appendix C Full Benchmark Results ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Tables</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and <a href="#A4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Twice the training budget. ‣ Appendix D Stability across Pretraining Runs ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> and in
the draft quality that <a href="#S4" title="4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> converts into decode speedup.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.24766v1/family_trainloss_toplegend.svg" id="A5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/205;" width="476" height="205"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>The same two terms across both families, over the steps all five runs share.
ECHO-1.5<sup id="A5.F6.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A5.F6.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup>’s event files start at step 60k on our side and the first thousand of
those go to the moving average’s warm-up, which fixes the window at 61k–78k; the
full-run view of the depth-1 pair is <a href="#A5.F5" title="In Appendix E Next-Token Loss Does Not Separate the Two Objectives ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>. On the backbone term (left) the
five lie within <math id="A5.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.006" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.006</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.006</annotation></semantics></math> and the ordering follows the family rather than the depth; the
depth-1 term (right) is where added depth shows up.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The same holds along depth.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A5.F6" title="In Appendix E Next-Token Loss Does Not Separate the Two Objectives ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> repeats the split for all
five configurations, ECHO-1, ECHO-1.5<sup id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> and ECHO-3 against MTP-1 and MTP-3, over the
steps all the runs share. Within a family the backbone term barely moves with depth: the three ECHO
configurations end within <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.002</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.002</annotation></semantics></math> of each other, and MTP-3 sits <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0017" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0017</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0017</annotation></semantics></math> below MTP-1. Across all
five it spans <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.006" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.006</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.006</annotation></semantics></math>, and the ordering is not ours to like — MTP-3 holds the lowest backbone
loss of any configuration, <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.676" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.676</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.676</annotation></semantics></math> against ECHO-3’s <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.682" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.682</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.682</annotation></semantics></math>, while ECHO-3 leads it by <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.97</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.97</annotation></semantics></math>
points over the fourteen benchmarks of <a href="#A3.T1" title="In Appendix C Full Benchmark Results ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. What does move is the MTP
term, and it moves the way the weighting predicts: the per-step loss is averaged over the depths
trained at that step, so adding depths takes weight off depth 1, and the depth-1 term rises by
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.027" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.027</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.027</annotation></semantics></math> from ECHO-1.5<sup id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> to ECHO-3 and by <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.048</annotation></semantics></math> from MTP-1 to MTP-3. At matched depth 3
the two designs divide the horizons: reusing the final layer fits the nearest one better
(<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.902" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.902</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.902</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.911" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.911</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.911</annotation></semantics></math>) and the separate modules fit the far ones better (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.992" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.992</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.992</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.045" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.045</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.045</annotation></semantics></math>
against <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.002</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.002</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.083" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.083</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.083</annotation></semantics></math> at depths 2 and 3). ECHO-1.5<sup id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup>’s deeper terms are logged only
on the steps that sample them, <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="39.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>39.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> of steps for depths 2 and 3, which is the
<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{k}=\mathbb{P}(D\geq k)=(1,0.4,0.1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{k}=\mathbb{P}(D\geq k)=(1,0.4,0.1)</annotation></semantics></math> that <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi=(0.6,0.3,0.1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi=(0.6,0.3,0.1)</annotation></semantics></math> prescribes in
<a href="#S4.E4" title="In DDS aligns training with speculative decoding. ‣ 4.1 Training Shallow, Drafting Deep ‣ 4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. At matched step those sampled depths are where the saving is paid for:
<a href="#A8.F7" title="In Appendix H Comparability of Reported Baselines in Inference ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> puts ECHO-1.5<sup id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup>’s depth-2 term <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.051" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.051</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.051</annotation></semantics></math> above ECHO-3’s at step 78k
and its depth-3 term <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.132" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.132</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.132</annotation></semantics></math> above, with the curves running parallel rather than converging.
That is the shape of the trade, and it stops there. Depth 1, which both train at every step,
costs nothing at all (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.874</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.902" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.902</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.902</annotation></semantics></math>, in ECHO-1.5<sup id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup>’s favour); the fourteen-task
average is within <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.02</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.02</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="36.34" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>36.34</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36.34</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="36.36" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>36.36</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36.36</annotation></semantics></math>, <a href="#A3.T1" title="In Appendix C Full Benchmark Results ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>); and the
accepted length holds beyond the trained depth (<a href="#S1.F1.sf2" title="In Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1(b)</span></a>). None of these margins is
where the comparison is settled, which is this
section’s point: the terms of the training objective do not rank the two designs.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>After Supervised Finetuning</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The pretrained checkpoints were finetuned on the chat SFT corpus, and
<a href="#A6.T3" title="In Appendix F After Supervised Finetuning ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> reports the fourteen in-scope benchmarks for the two ECHO
configurations against DeepSeek’s MTP baseline finetuned the same way.
ECHO keeps its lead after
finetuning, <math id="A6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.61" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.61</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.61</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+2.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2.10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+2.10</annotation></semantics></math> points over the fourteen rows, and the
lead is again larger on reasoning and code than on QA and multiple choice.
Three caveats apply. The cells are decoded greedily, so
repeating an evaluation does not move the rule- and execution-graded rows, and no
error bars are drawn for them. The four judge-graded rows, BBEH and the three
closed-book sets, do carry grader variability.
BBH is read in its chain-of-thought form: under the answer-directly prompt the
finetuned output degenerates to a constant option label.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T3" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A6.T3.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="A6.T3.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T3.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">Category</td>
<td id="A6.T3.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">Benchmark</td>
<td id="A6.T3.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">MTP-Instruct</td>
<td id="A6.T3.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">ECHO-1.5<sup id="A6.T3.2.1.4.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T3.2.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup>-Instruct</td>
<td id="A6.T3.2.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">ECHO-2<sup id="A6.T3.2.1.5.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A6.T3.2.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(7)</span></sup>-Instruct</td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T3.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T3.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;" rowspan="2"><span id="A6.T3.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Mathematics</span></td>
<td id="A6.T3.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">GSM8K</td>
<td id="A6.T3.2.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">61.87</td>
<td id="A6.T3.2.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">62.70</td>
<td id="A6.T3.2.2.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">65.20</td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T3.2.3" class="ltx_tr">

<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Decode Speedup under Serving</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A9.F8" title="In Appendix I Artifact Licensing ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> reports the cells of <a href="#S3.F3.sf2" title="In Figure 3 ‣ Sharing promotes longer-horizon supervision. ‣ 3.1 Direct Multi-Horizon Supervision via Final-Layer Sharing ‣ 3 ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(b)</span></a> as decode speedup instead of accepted length; the ordering of the drafters is the one discussed in <a href="#S4" title="4 Pushing the Frontier of Speculative Decoding under Realistic Serving ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Comparability of Reported Baselines in Inference</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The evaluation scales differ systematically. EAGLE-3 reports results across a wide range of target sizes, from Vicuna-13B up to LLaMA-3.3-70B, whereas the parallel drafters cluster at the small end: Domino <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2026</a>)</cite> evaluates only Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, DSpark extends to Qwen3-14B, and the largest target any of them reports is Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, a sparse model with roughly 3B active parameters, so its per-token cost is closer to a 4B dense model than to a 30B one. No paper in this family evaluates a dense target above 14B (<a href="#A8.T4" title="In Appendix H Comparability of Reported Baselines in Inference ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).</p>
</div>

<td id="A8.T4.2.1.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="A8.T4.2.1.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B80000;">✗</span></td>

</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="A8.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond scale, the EAGLE-3 checkpoints these papers evaluate were never fairly trained (<a href="#A8.T5" title="In Appendix H Comparability of Reported Baselines in Inference ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). DFlash and Domino used public checkpoints released by AngelSlim with the different training datasets and fewer samples. Drafter capacity is uncontrolled as well: at every target, the block-parallel drafter carries <math id="A8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.1</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A8.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2.6\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.6\times</annotation></semantics></math> the parameters of the EAGLE-3 head.</p>
</div>

<div id="A8.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Although DSpark controls the data axis: it retrains EAGLE-3 and DSpark within a single framework on identical training dataset, however, its evaluation restricts EAGLE-3 to chain drafting instead of the original tree drafting. The released code proposes one token per step and returns a single trajectory with no tree construction, top-k expansion, or candidate reranking. The baseline is therefore matched in data but evaluated in a degraded configuration, and its acceptance length understates what the method achieves as published.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.24766v1/depth2_by_step_ZCR.svg" id="A8.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:329/239;" width="329" height="239"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span>The depth-2 term at matched pretraining step. ECHO-1.5<sup id="A8.F7.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A8.F7.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(3)</span></sup> samples depth 2 on
<math id="A8.F7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="39.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>39.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> of steps where ECHO-3 trains it on all of them, so the sampled series carries fewer
points over this window, <math id="A8.F7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6{,}721" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6,721</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6{,}721</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="A8.F7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>. Fewer is not biased: at depth 1,
which both configurations train every step, the loss on the steps that also sample depth 2
differs from the loss on the steps that do not by <math id="A8.F7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0002</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0002</annotation></semantics></math>, against a standard error of
<math id="A8.F7.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0004" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0004</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0004</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>

<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A9.T6" title="In Appendix I Artifact Licensing ‣ ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion BeyondAuxiliary Multi-Token Prediction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> summarizes the
licenses and usage terms of the training and
evaluation datasets used in our experiments.
The pretraining corpus and in-house SFT dataset
are proprietary and subject to restricted
redistribution. All fourteen evaluation benchmarks
are used solely for research evaluation and are
not redistributed.
The use of these artifacts follows their applicable
licenses and access conditions.</p>
</div>

<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>AI Use Disclosure</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">During the preparation of this manuscript, the authors used ChatGPT (OpenAI) to assist with language editing, grammatical corrections, and improving the clarity of author-written text. The AI tool was not used to generate research findings or experimental results. All AI-assisted modifications were reviewed and verified by the authors, who take full responsibility for the content of this manuscript.</p>
</div>
</section>
